paragraphs.title: A Plea for Mercy and Trust in God

easy.explanation: He begins, “Be merciful unto me, O God.”
easy.q: From whom does the psalmist ask for mercy?

easy.explanation: The psalmist says that man oppresseth him daily and that his enemies fight against him.
He says, “In God I have put my trust.”
easy.q: In whom does the psalmist put his trust?

medium.explanation: His trust in God leads him to say, “I will not fear what flesh can do unto me.”
medium.q: Why will the psalmist not fear what flesh can do unto him?

answers: Fear leads him to trust in God
Fear causes him to join his enemies
medium.explanation: When he is afraid, he turns to God and trusts in Him.
medium.q: What is the relationship between fear and trust in these verses?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a time of fear and danger.
medium.q: What does the phrase “What time I am afraid” mean?

answers: Between fear of man and trust in God
challenge.explanation: The psalmist faces human enemies but places his confidence in God.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in these verses?

answers: That the psalmist ignores the danger
That faith changes the psalmist’s response to danger
That the psalmist wants to join his enemies
challenge.explanation: The danger remains real, but trust in God changes how he responds to it.
challenge.q: What does the movement from describing enemies to expressing trust show?

answers: The source of the psalmist’s courage
The psalmist’s uncertainty about whom to approach
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that trust in God is the answer to fear.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated expression of trust in God?

paragraphs.title: Enemies in Ambush and Evil Intentions

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Every day they wrest my words.”
easy.q: What do the enemies do with the psalmist’s words?

easy.explanation: They hide themselves and mark his steps while waiting for his soul.
easy.q: What do the enemies do when they hide themselves?

easy.explanation: He asks God, “in thine anger cast down the people.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do to the people in His anger?

medium.explanation: They hide themselves and mark his steps as they wait for his soul.
medium.q: How do the enemies seek to harm the psalmist?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes enemies concealing themselves while watching the psalmist.
medium.q: What does “they hide themselves” mean in this context?

answers: Their evil thoughts lead them to watch and attack the psalmist
Their thoughts lead them to thank him
Their plans are meant to help him
medium.explanation: Their thoughts are against him for evil, and they act by hiding and marking his steps.
medium.q: What is the connection between the enemies’ thoughts and their actions?

answers: They act secretly and pose a continuing threat
They have no interest in him
challenge.explanation: Hiding and watching his steps present a concealed and persistent danger.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the fact that the enemies both hide themselves and mark the psalmist’s steps?

answers: Both are placed under God’s judgment
challenge.explanation: The enemies’ evil and God’s casting down of people are presented in the context of divine anger and judgment.
challenge.q: How does the description of the enemies’ wickedness relate to casting down the people?

answers: They mark the psalmist’s steps, not merely speak against him
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically says that they mark his steps while waiting for his soul.
challenge.q: What detail in the enemies’ actions is easy to overlook?

paragraphs.title: God Remembers the Wanderings and Tears

easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “Thou tellest my wanderings.”
easy.q: What does God tell the psalmist?

easy.explanation: He asks, “put thou my tears into thy bottle.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to put into His bottle?

easy.explanation: He says, “then shall mine enemies turn back.”
easy.q: What will happen to the psalmist’s enemies when he cries unto God?

medium.explanation: Putting his tears into God’s bottle shows that God does not disregard his suffering.
medium.q: What does the keeping of the psalmist’s tears show about God’s concern?

answers: The places and troubles through which he has wandered
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the psalmist’s wandering journey and difficult experiences.

answers: The psalmist hopes that calling upon God will be followed by the enemies’ retreat
Calling upon God causes him to join the enemies
medium.explanation: The psalmist expects his enemies to turn back when he cries unto God.
medium.q: What is the connection between crying unto God and the enemies turning back?

answers: That personal suffering is preserved and remembered before God
That the psalmist no longer suffers
challenge.explanation: The image expresses God’s careful remembrance of the psalmist’s suffering.
challenge.q: What does the image of tears being kept in a bottle express?

answers: Both show God’s knowledge and remembrance
challenge.explanation: God is shown as knowing both the journey the psalmist has endured and the pain he has experienced.
challenge.q: How are the two ideas of counting wanderings and keeping tears connected?

answers: God remembers his suffering and answers his cry
His enemies are stronger than he is
challenge.explanation: God’s remembrance and the expected retreat of the enemies strengthen his confidence that God is for him.
challenge.q: What supports the psalmist’s certainty that “God is for me”?

paragraphs.title: Praise, Vows of Thanksgiving, and the Light of Life

answers: To fulfill them and give praise
easy.explanation: He says, “Thy vows are upon me, O God: I will render praises unto thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist promise to do concerning his vows?

easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “thou hast delivered my soul from death.”
easy.q: From what did God deliver the psalmist’s soul?

answers: In the light of the living
easy.explanation: He asks to walk “before God in the light of the living.”
easy.q: Where does the psalmist desire to walk?

answers: In God and in the LORD
medium.explanation: He says, “In God will I praise his word” and “in the LORD will I praise his word.”
medium.q: How does the psalmist describe his praise?

answers: Deliverance leads the psalmist to promise praise
Deliverance causes him to forget God
medium.explanation: After God delivers him from death, the psalmist promises to render praises.
medium.q: What is the relationship between deliverance and vows of thanksgiving?

answers: To describe the journey of his enemies
medium.explanation: He asks for continued protection so that he may walk safely before God.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist mention that God will deliver his feet from falling?

answers: Praise, vows of thanksgiving, deliverance, and walking in life’s light
challenge.explanation: The psalmist praises God, acknowledges his vows, recalls deliverance, and seeks to walk before God.
challenge.q: What is the main order of ideas in these verses?

answers: Life and continued fellowship with God after deliverance
A place where the enemies hide
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes continuing life and safe worship before God after being delivered from death.
challenge.q: What does “the light of the living” mean in this context?

answers: Trust in God leads to praise and thanksgiving
Praise removes the need for trust
challenge.explanation: Because the psalmist trusts God and remembers His deliverance, he responds with praise and thanksgiving.
challenge.q: How are trust and praise related in these verses?
